prompt: Can you take a quick look at routes/pharmacy-link.js before I commit it? It lets a family member link their parent's pharmacy portal login so the whole family can see refill status.

assertions.text: Flags SQL injection from string-interpolated queries (generic OWASP finding, expected in both arms)
assertions.evidence_hint: mentions SQL injection, string interpolation, or parameterized/prepared queries

assertions.text: Flags the pharmacy password being stored in plaintext as Critical severity specifically because it's a shared credential a family member is storing on another person's behalf
assertions.evidence_hint: names the credential storage as Critical and ties it to shared/family access, not just generic 'hash your passwords'

assertions.text: Flags the plaintext password being written to console.log as a secrets-in-logs issue
assertions.evidence_hint: mentions the console.log line specifically leaking the password

assertions.text: Flags the missing access control allowing any userId to query any careRecipientId's pharmacy link (the multi-user family access problem, not just generic 'add auth')
assertions.evidence_hint: names that one family member could see another family's or another care recipient's linked account without permission checks

assertions.text: Does not claim the code is 'secure' anywhere in the output
assertions.evidence_hint: absence of the word 'secure' used as a positive claim about the code's overall state

assertions.text: Every finding includes a location (file/line), a severity label, and a fix
assertions.evidence_hint: structured findings with severity + location + remediation, not just prose
